div.head: II Eg 2.3
div.ab: ⁊ gelæste man sulhælmessan, þonne XVniht beon onufan eastran.
Gelæste man sulhælmessan, þonne XV niht beon onufan eastran.
Gelæste man sulhælmessan þonne XV niht beon onufan eastran.
And gelæste man sulhælmessan, þonne XV niht beon onufan Eastran.
(Und man leiste Pflugalmosen, wenn 15 Nächte [14 Tage vergangen] sind über Ostern. A D)
(And let plough-alms be paid when it is 15 nights [a fortnight] after Easter. A D)
Plough-alms shall be rendered 15 days after Easter.
[And plough-alms are to be rendered when it is 15 days after Easter.]
Plow dues are to be paid on the fifteenth night after Easter.

Plow dues . . . Easter: This clause was likely added by Wulfstan. For the dues in this and the following clauses, see the notes to The Laws of Edward and Guthrum 6.3, Canons 54, 5 Æthelred 12, and The Obligations of Individuals 3.4.

note.seg: 2, 3 bringt Cnut 8, 1 ebenfalls vor II Eg. 3.
Cnut 8, 1 likewise places 2, 3 before II Eg. 3.

Dieser Satz der Rec. II, obwohl von V Atr 11, 1 = VI 16 = VIII 12 = I Cn 8, 1 ebenfalls vor den mit II Eg 3 gleichen Inhalt gesetzt, gehört nicht dem Urtext (so auch Schmid 187). Dieser lässt vielmehr in geschlossenerem Zusammenhang auf Zehnt und Kirchenpfennig deren Termine folgen

This sentence of Rec. II, although V Atr 11, 1 = VI 16 = VIII 12 = I Cn 8, 1 likewise place it before the matter corresponding to II Eg 3, does not belong to the original text (so also Schmid 187). The original text, rather, in a more closely connected sequence, makes the dates for tithe and church-scot follow upon those two
Schmid and Liebermann agree that this clause is an addition to the original text, cf. cap. 5, 2 f.

Liebermann takes this phrase to mean a fortnight and compares it with Hn. 41, 2 a; 59, 2 b where the series 7 days, 15 days, 3 weeks, 4 weeks is found, but may not these be due to French reckoning? The ordinary expression for two weeks in England must have been feowertyne niht from the beginning. The reason for 15 here may be that dues were not to be paid on a Sunday.
